accepted.s: The term ‘disinvestment’ was introduced in the Indian policy framework through which of the following?
accepted.x: The term ‘disinvestment’ was introduced in the Interim Budget presented in July 1991.
accepted.tq: Use the exact year and policy document rather than associating the term with a later committee.
accepted.sec: ■ Disinvestment policy - committees, Disinvestment Commission, DIPAM, starting year  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the first round of disinvestment in India, consider the following statements:
1. It was undertaken during 1991–92.
2. Minority stakes in 31 public sector undertakings were offered.
3. A disinvestment limit of 20 per cent was announced.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The first round of disinvestment took place in 1991–92, involved minority stakes in 31 PSUs and announced a 20 per cent disinvestment limit.
accepted.tq: Combine the date, number of enterprises and percentage in one statement set.
accepted.sec: ■ Disinvestment policy - committees, Disinvestment Commission, DIPAM, starting year  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Rangarajan Committee, constituted in 1993, recommended which of the following regarding disinvestment?
o: Retention of at least 74 per cent government ownership in every PSU
Complete privatisation of all public sector undertakings
A ban on strategic sales of public enterprises
Disinvestment up to 49 per cent in PSUs reserved for the public sector
accepted.x: The Rangarajan Committee recommended disinvestment up to 49 per cent in PSUs reserved for the public sector. It also suggested up to 74 per cent disinvestment in other enterprises.
accepted.tq: Test the committee’s recommendation through the specific percentage associated with it.
accepted.sec: ■ Disinvestment policy - committees, Disinvestment Commission, DIPAM, starting year  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: V. Krishnamurthy Committee — 1991 — Early disinvestment approach
Disinvestment Commission — 1993 — Faster disinvestment and governance reforms
Vijay Kelkar Committee — 1984 — PSU autonomy and MoUs
accepted.x: The V. Krishnamurthy Committee of 1991 represented an early approach to disinvestment. The other pairs confuse the years or functions of different bodies.
accepted.tq: Match each committee with its year and distinctive policy contribution.
accepted.sec: ■ Disinvestment policy - committees, Disinvestment Commission, DIPAM, starting year  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Disinvestment Commission established in 1996 was headed initially by
accepted.x: G.V. Ramakrishna was the first Chairperson of the Disinvestment Commission, established in 1996.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the chairperson of the Commission from the chairpersons of the recommendation committees.
accepted.sec: ■ Disinvestment policy - committees, Disinvestment Commission, DIPAM, starting year  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The principal recommendation associated with the Disinvestment Commission headed by G.V. Ramakrishna was
o: Replacement of MRTP by the Competition Act
Transfer of all PSUs to State Governments
Case-by-case advice on sale of public enterprises
accepted.x: The Disinvestment Commission provided case-by-case advice on the sale of public enterprises and recommended strategic sales.
accepted.tq: Identify the body from its distinctive recommendation rather than from its establishment year alone.
accepted.sec: ■ Disinvestment policy - committees, Disinvestment Commission, DIPAM, starting year  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Department of Disinvestment was later renamed as DIPAM in
accepted.x: The Department of Disinvestment was renamed the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) in 2016.
accepted.tq: Use the renaming year to separate the department’s creation from its later institutional transformation.
accepted.sec: ■ Disinvestment policy - committees, Disinvestment Commission, DIPAM, starting year  [APPSC]

accepted.s: DIPAM functions under the Ministry of Finance and is concerned primarily with
o: Managing Central Government equity and disinvestment
Regulating foreign exchange markets and monetary policy
accepted.x: DIPAM, under the Ministry of Finance, manages Central Government equity and disinvestment in public assets.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the responsible department.
accepted.sec: ■ Disinvestment policy - committees, Disinvestment Commission, DIPAM, starting year  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a method or instrument managed in the context of Central Government disinvestment by DIPAM?
accepted.x: Strategic sale, Offer for Sale, IPO/FPO and CPSE ETF are disinvestment-related instruments. Statutory liquidity ratio is a monetary and banking instrument, not a disinvestment method.
accepted.tq: Find the one item belonging to monetary policy rather than public-asset management.
accepted.sec: ■ Disinvestment policy - committees, Disinvestment Commission, DIPAM, starting year  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following phases of disinvestment in chronological order:
A. First strategic sales
B. Minority sales
C. Period in which about 70 per cent of cumulative proceeds since 1991 were realised
accepted.x: Minority sales characterised 1991–98, first strategic sales occurred during 1999–2004, and the period from 2014 onwards accounted for about 70 per cent of cumulative proceeds since 1991.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest phase and then place the later strategic-sale phase.
accepted.sec: ■ Disinvestment policy - committees, Disinvestment Commission, DIPAM, starting year  [APPSC]

accepted.s: During the phase from 1991 to 1998, the approximate amount realised through minority disinvestment was
accepted.x: Minority disinvestment during 1991–98 realised approximately ₹17,557 crore.
accepted.tq: Test the exact phase-wise realisation using closely spaced numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: ■ Disinvestment policy - committees, Disinvestment Commission, DIPAM, starting year  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was associated with PSU autonomy and Memoranda of Understanding rather than with the disinvestment policy recommendations?
accepted.x: Arjun Sengupta’s 1984 work was associated with PSU autonomy and Memoranda of Understanding, not with the later disinvestment recommendations.
accepted.tq: Separate a nearby but distinct reform theme from the committees directly concerned with disinvestment.

accepted.s: The MRTP Act, 1969 was primarily enacted to
o: Control private monopolies and concentration of economic power
Promote unrestricted concentration of economic power
Provide financial assistance to public enterprises
accepted.x: The MRTP Act sought to control private monopolies and concentration of economic power and to curb monopolistic, restrictive and unfair trade practices.
accepted.tq: Use the purpose of the statute to distinguish it from laws dealing with public finance or foreign exchange.
accepted.sec: ■ MRTP Act 1969 - purpose, recommending committee, replacing law  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The MRTP Act, 1969 was recommended by the
accepted.x: The Dutt Committee, formally the Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee, recommended the MRTP legislation.
accepted.tq: Trap the closely associated Hazari and Dutt committees by asking which one made the recommendation.
accepted.sec: ■ MRTP Act 1969 - purpose, recommending committee, replacing law  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the MRTP Act:
1. It was enacted in 1969.
2. It became effective in 1970.
3. It was replaced by the Competition Act, 2002.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The MRTP Act was enacted in 1969, came into effect in 1970 and was subsequently replaced by the Competition Act, 2002.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the enactment year from the effective year and the later replacement law.
accepted.sec: ■ MRTP Act 1969 - purpose, recommending committee, replacing law  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The MRTP Commission was replaced by the
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
accepted.x: The MRTP Commission was replaced by the Competition Commission of India (CCI) under the competition-law framework.
accepted.tq: Match the abolished statutory body with its institutional successor.
accepted.sec: ■ MRTP Act 1969 - purpose, recommending committee, replacing law  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the change in the MRTP firm threshold?
o: The asset limit fell from ₹100 crore to ₹20 crore in 1985, while the market-share threshold rose from 25 per cent to 33 per cent in 1984.
The asset limit rose from ₹20 crore to ₹100 crore in 1985, while the market-share threshold was reduced from 33 per cent to 25 per cent in 1984.
Both the asset limit and the market-share threshold were reduced in 1984.
Both the asset limit and the market-share threshold were raised in 1985.
accepted.x: An MRTP firm was initially associated with assets of ₹20 crore or more or a 33 per cent market share. The market-share threshold was reduced to 25 per cent in 1984, and the asset limit was raised to ₹100 crore in 1985.
accepted.tq: Track the direction and year of each threshold change separately.
accepted.sec: ■ MRTP Act 1969 - purpose, recommending committee, replacing law  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes disinvestment from privatisation?
o: Disinvestment removes licences and quotas, whereas privatisation integrates the economy with the world economy.
Disinvestment always transfers management control, whereas privatisation may retain government control.
Disinvestment means sale of all government assets, whereas privatisation means sale of only minority shares.
Disinvestment reduces government equity, while privatisation transfers ownership and management control to the private sector.
accepted.x: Disinvestment is the sale or reduction of government equity, with the government possibly retaining majority ownership and control. Privatisation involves transfer of ownership and management control to the private sector.
accepted.tq: Separate the two look-alike terms by asking whether ownership and management control are transferred.
accepted.sec: ■ LPG terminology - disinvestment vs privatisation vs liberalisation vs globalisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Removal of licences, quotas and controls, with the State acting mainly as a facilitator, is known as
accepted.x: Liberalisation refers to removing licences, quotas and controls and changing the State’s role from controller to facilitator.
accepted.tq: Identify the LPG term from its defining policy action rather than from ownership changes.
accepted.sec: ■ LPG terminology - disinvestment vs privatisation vs liberalisation vs globalisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Integration of the Indian economy with the world economy through tariff cuts, FDI and the transition from FERA to FEMA is termed
accepted.x: Globalisation denotes integration with the world economy and includes measures such as tariff reduction, FDI and the shift from FERA to FEMA.
accepted.tq: Use the policy instruments listed in the description to identify the correct LPG concept.
accepted.sec: ■ LPG terminology - disinvestment vs privatisation vs liberalisation vs globalisation

accepted.s: A government retains more than 51 per cent equity and control in a public sector enterprise while selling a part of its holding. This is called
accepted.x: Under minority disinvestment, the government retains more than 51 per cent ownership and control. Majority disinvestment transfers control while retaining a minority stake.
accepted.tq: Apply the percentage and control test to distinguish minority and majority disinvestment.
accepted.sec: ■ LPG terminology - disinvestment vs privatisation vs liberalisation vs globalisation

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the corresponding government stake or control?
o: Minority disinvestment — government retains more than 51 per cent and control
Majority disinvestment — government retains more than 51 per cent and control
Complete privatisation — government retains a controlling stake
Strategic sale — no transfer of management control
accepted.x: Minority disinvestment leaves the government with more than 51 per cent and control. Majority disinvestment transfers control, while complete privatisation transfers 100 per cent ownership and control.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure ownership-and-control pair and eliminate the reversed descriptions.
accepted.sec: ■ LPG terminology - disinvestment vs privatisation vs liberalisation vs globalisation

accepted.s: A strategic sale generally involves
o: Transfer of all public assets to another government department
Sale of exactly 10 per cent of shares without any change in management
Sale of a block of shares, usually 50 per cent or more, along with transfer of management control
Removal of industrial licences without any sale of equity
accepted.x: A strategic sale normally involves a block of shares, usually 50 per cent or more, together with transfer of management control to a strategic partner.
accepted.tq: Test the defining combination of a substantial share block and management control.
accepted.sec: ■ LPG terminology - disinvestment vs privatisation vs liberalisation vs globalisation

accepted.s: The Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 primarily provided for
o: Transfer of management of all industries to foreign investors
Regulation of agricultural land ceilings alone
Licensing for starting or expanding industrial units and the creation of Development Councils
Abolition of all industrial licences and quotas
accepted.x: The IDRA, 1951 provided for licensing of industrial units when they were started or expanded and also provided for Development Councils. It was amended in 1953.
accepted.tq: Identify the Act from its two core functions instead of confusing it with later liberalisation measures.
accepted.sec: ■ Industrial licensing - IDRA 1951, Hazari and Dutt committees, number licensed  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 was amended in
accepted.x: The IDRA, 1951 was amended in 1953.
accepted.tq: Test the amendment year separately from the year of enactment.
accepted.sec: ■ Industrial licensing - IDRA 1951, Hazari and Dutt committees, number licensed  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Hazari Report of 1967 and the Dutt Committee of 1969 exposed the fact that industrial licensing
o: Was confined exclusively to public sector enterprises
Had eliminated concentration of economic power
accepted.x: The Hazari Report and Dutt Committee found that the licensing system tended to favour large business houses, contributing to the subsequent MRTP framework.
accepted.tq: Link the reports to their common finding rather than confusing their dates with the MRTP enactment year.
accepted.sec: ■ Industrial licensing - IDRA 1951, Hazari and Dutt committees, number licensed  [other exams]

accepted.x: During the 1980s, 32 industrial groups were delicensed.

accepted.s: The negative list announced in 1988 contained how many industries?
accepted.x: The negative list of 1988 contained 26 industries.

accepted.s:
Which of the following industries were among the three additional sectors delicensed in 1993?
1. Automobiles
2. White goods
3. Leather
4. Industrial explosives
accepted.x: Automobiles, white goods and leather were the three sectors delicensed in 1993. Industrial explosives remained among the industries subject to compulsory licensing.
accepted.tq: Separate the three-item 1993 delicensing group from the later retained licensing categories.
accepted.sec: ■ Industrial licensing - IDRA 1951, Hazari and Dutt committees, number licensed  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly presents the later sequence of delicensing measures?
o: Electronic goods in December 1996/July 1997, followed by coal and petroleum in Budget 1998–99
Coal and petroleum in December 1996/July 1997, followed by electronic goods in Budget 1998–99
Leather in Budget 1998–99, followed by automobiles in December 1996/July 1997
Industrial explosives in 1993, followed by hazardous chemicals in 1996
accepted.x: Electronic goods were delicensed in December 1996/July 1997, and coal and petroleum were delicensed in the 1998–99 Budget.
accepted.tq: Arrange the policy steps by using the dated milestones rather than the sector names alone.
accepted.sec: ■ Industrial licensing - IDRA 1951, Hazari and Dutt committees, number licensed  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the five industries that continued under compulsory licensing?
accepted.x: The five remaining categories were alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, electronic aerospace and defence equipment, and industrial explosives. Leather had been delicensed in 1993.
accepted.tq: Find the sector removed from the final compulsory-licensing list by recalling the earlier delicensing step.
